title: Iris and the Missing Sparkle Skipper
markdown:
Iris the iguana blinked her bright curious eyes. Dawn poked its golden fingers through the jungle canopy, painting her emerald scales with brilliant streaks of yellow. The jungle air buzzed with promise. Every day she glided across the cool still water of the underground lake in her trusty Sparkle Skipper, the fastest little boat on the water. It bobbed and bounced with every gentle ripple, bright blue paint shimmering. She paddled past sleeping fish and dove for smooth skipping stones.

Today the special spot by the lake felt empty. Not a speck of sparkly blue paint. Not a tiny tugboat flag fluttering. The Sparkle Skipper was gone. A tremor rippled through Iris’s whiskers. A boat-shaped problem. She bounced on the balls of her feet, a determined glint in her eye.

Then a frantic tapping started at her window. Tap-tap-tap. Tiny pebbles against the glass. Iris dashed over, heart thumping. Boon the bat, velvet wings a blur against the bright morning sky, swooped and circled. "Iris. Iris. I saw it. Your boat. It floated away. Pulled by glowing mushrooms." He pointed a tiny leathery claw toward a patch of dim earth near the cave entrance, a place Iris usually avoided. "They were practically dancing. Pulsing and glowing."

Glowing mushrooms. Her boat. A proper puzzling adventure. Her emerald scales seemed to glow a little brighter. "They cannot be far, Boon. Adventure calls."

Boon blinked his big round eyes. "Into the dark cave?" His voice quivered just a tiny bit.

"Do not worry." Iris grabbed her trusty explorer’s hat, a bright red cap with a particularly bouncy feather. "You have your echo-peeps, and I have my brave heart. We will be great together."

They dashed toward the cave entrance. The air inside was immediately cooler, a welcome change from the jungle heat. Boon took a deep gulping breath, let out a series of rapid peep-peeps that shot out like tiny sonic bullets, and instantly a vivid map of the cave appeared in his sharp mind. "This way." A streak of black velvet, he flew ahead.

The path twisted and turned like a giant serpent’s tail. Strange drips echoed, tiny secret whispers. The air grew damp and cool, smelling of wet earth and something sweet. Giant bulbous mushrooms, pulsing with a soft blue-green light, lined the tunnel. They bobbed gently, as if beckoning them forward, their glow casting dancing shadows. Click-clack went Iris’s claws on the rocky floor. Boon zipped and zoomed, echo-peeps bouncing off every rock, showing them exactly where the path dipped or rose.

They burst into a massive cavern. Sunlight, filtered through a hidden crack high in the ceiling, streamed down like a gigantic golden spotlight. And there it was. The Sparkle Skipper, bobbing merrily on a shimmering pool right next to a tumbling splashing waterfall. Guarding it were tiny giggling sprites, mischievous grins from ear to ear, outfits spun from moonlight. One sprite, wings like a dragonfly, tickled the boat’s tiny sail with a long thin reed.

"Hey." Iris’s voice was clear and indignant. "That is my boat. What are you doing?"

The sprites giggled louder, laughter echoing like tiny bells. Tiny hands as light as spider silk brushed the sail, and a faint sweet scent of moon-blossoms wafted through the air. "We borrowed it," one squeaked, hopping up and down. "It looked so sparkly and fast."

Iris looked at her precious boat, then at the mischievous sprites, then at her own dazzling green scales, which were catching the spotlight and practically exploding with colour. A brilliant bold idea sparked. "What if you can borrow my sparkle? I will trade you some dazzling green shine for my boat." She puffed out her chest, scales shimmering magnificently, shifting through every shade of emerald and jade.

The sprites gasped. They had never seen such brilliant green. "Deal," they chirped in unison. With a final happy splash they pushed the Sparkle Skipper toward Iris. The sprites gathered around, mesmerized, marveling at the dazzling shifting colours, giggling with pure delight.

Iris and Boon paddled the Sparkle Skipper back to the familiar welcoming waters of the underground lake. "That was spectacular," Boon chirped, doing a little loop-de-loop. Iris grinned, emerald scales glinting in the soft light of the lake’s glow-worms. With a happy splash they set off to explore more of their wondrous world, the Sparkle Skipper’s tiny flag fluttering as if it had only been on holiday.
